audit.note: the pressed tile's header or tooltip and the press action travel with every tile press

deviations.what: three post-1.71 members are kept for the 1:1 port: sap.m.GenericTile.linkTileContents (the property and the aggregation, both @since 1.120) and the control sap.m.LinkTileContent it holds (@since 1.120). The app needs a UI5 release >= 1.120; below it the lowercase linkTileContents tag resolves as a control class and the 404 takes the whole view down, which is why this is an error rather than a warning.

changeEnforceSmall does model.setProperty('/sizeBehavior', state ? 'Small' : 'Responsive'). Both halves are bindable, so the Switch's state and the seven sizeBehavior bindings share one round trip that writes one field - the same two values the original writes. The ComboBox's selectedKey and every scope binding likewise share the /scope field the sample already binds, so switching the tile actions needs no handler at all: that is what the sample's own {/scope} binding does.

press and pressSlideTile compose their toast from the pressed tile (getHeader() || getTooltip()) and from the press action, and say 'Remove action of ...' when the action is Remove. Both travel: the wire carries ${$source>/header} (or ${$source>/tooltip} for the news tiles) and ${$parameters>/action}, and the backend composes the same two sentences. The two SlideTiles pass their own tooltip literally, since that is what the handler reads for them.
onLinkPress toasts the constant 'Pressed on Link', so it is wired round-trip-free as follow_up_action( control_global, MESSAGE_TOAST show ) (app 005 idiom).

the tiles' state binding is {= ${state} || 'Loaded' } in the sample - the mock leaves state absent on two of the five tiles and empty on the news tiles. A flat ABAP row would send an empty string into the LoadState enum, so the fallback is applied at SEED time instead: the absent and empty states are seeded 'Loaded', which is the value the expression produces. The three the mock does set (Loading, Failed, Disabled) are carried verbatim - they are what the sample shows.

tiles.json carries slideTile1 and slideTile2 as two arrays of the SAME shape and the same length, so the data-fidelity gate could not tell which ABAP block belongs to which and compared both against slideTile1 until 2026-10-08; its matcher now also weighs which array holds the block's values and pairs each block with its own. The seeds are verbatim: t_slide1 is slideTile1 (NewsImage2 / 'August 22, 2016' / the NFL.com headline first) and t_slide2 is slideTile2 (NewsImage1 / 'August 21, 2016' / the Wind Map headline first), each with its own TOOLTIP ('NewsTile n of SlideTile 1' vs '... SlideTile 2'), BACKGROUNDIMAGE, FOOTER, CONTENTTEXT, SUBTITLE and STATE. Nothing here is changed from the mock beyond the two folds this sidecar already records - the host absolutization on BACKGROUNDIMAGE and the 'Loaded' seed for an empty STATE.

the four background images come from the sample's own images folder and point at the sdk.openui5.org host per the offline asset-URL rule; the mock writes them relative as 'test-resources/sap/m/demokit/sample/GenericTileLineMode/images/...'. The LinkTileContent hrefs stay the sample's own http://www.sap.com.

not yet verified in a running system: the LineMode row of tiles, the two auto-advancing SlideTiles, the scope switch and the Remove-action toast. **e2e-verified 2026-08-25** (nightly e2e interaction, meta/interactions/z2ui5_cl_smpc_app_606.mjs).
